items.detail: Seven vessel incidents Oct 11–13 (UKMTO): a crude tanker struck in outbound Hormuz transit, a UAV hit near Oman's Sohar anchorage, one tanker diverted to Fujairah; 6 of 14 transiting vessels ran dark. Hormuz flows averaged 10.5M b/d over 7 days, ~38% below prewar 17.1M b/d (Kpler). Average crude freight is $30/bbl vs $4 a year ago. The Brent-WTI front spread is $11.66; the WTI curve is in steep backwardation (Dec-26 94.05 → Dec-27 79.76, −16.1%). IEA-board G7 release details Wed–Thu Oct 14–15; a Hormuz reopening collapses the front, escalation spikes it. Binary — the market prices logistics risk, not barrel shortage.
items.title: Hormuz disruption is the dominant macro catalyst — crude backwardation prices logistics risk
